text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp said Wednesday test of the Monazite 1 well offshore Louisiana were inconclusive and the well has been abandoned.
Future appraisal drilling will be necessary to determine commerciality of the discovery, the company said.
The Gulf of Mexico sub-salt discovery, located on Vermilion South Addition Block 375, was drilled to 18,000 feet measured depth and 15,226 feet total vertical depth.
The well -- owned equally by Anadarko, Phillips Petroleum Co and Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd -- encountered multiple hydrocarbon-bearing sands.
The sands were confirmed by well logs, core analyses and production testing, Anadarko said, noting production tests were attempted over the past month on separate pay intervals.
While all test intervals flowed oil, data obtained were largely inconclusive due to various problems encountered during test operations including extensive sand production.
Due to wellbore conditions, this well has been plugged and abandoned, Anadarko said.
Over the next several months, existing seismic information will be revised using data obtained by the Monazite 1 well. Meanwhile, new seismic data are being obtained, Anadarko said.
